This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH5 2.

The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 01.08.2022 at about 8.45 a.m. he had been riding a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA04JH9154 near Nagarjun College, NH44 road, Hyderabad to Banga, Nandi Hobli, Chickballapura, a Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA39DU4396 came in high speed without observing any traffic rules and regulations inorder to overtake a Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA40A7095 dashed against back side his motor cycle, due to the said impact he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Jain Mission Hospital Chikkaballapur, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient, for which he has spent an amount of Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical and other expenses.
SCCH5 3.

At the time of the accident he was aged about 26 years, hale and healthy, working as factory worker, thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m., due to this accident he is unable to do his normal activities, he has lost his income and earning capacity.
Out of this accident crime No.110/2022
is registered against the driver of the Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA39DU4396 before the nandi Giridhama Police for the offences punishable under Sec. 279, 337 of IPC.
R1 is the owner, R2 is insurer of the said car, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.
On service of notice, R1/owner has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioner.
It is submitted that, driver of the Ertiga Car by name SCCH5 S.Shasha Vali was issued driving license in October 2010 and he was holding valid and effective driving license to drive the car.
Further denied age, occupation, income of the petitioner, occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by him.
Further submitted that, Ertiga car bearing Reg.No.AP39 DU4369 was insured with R2 for third party liabilities and was in force as on the date of accident.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.

sentences.text: Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. R2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioner.

He has issued policy bearing No.2311 2032 7760 4300 000 against the car bearing Engine No.1038020 and Chassis No.211629 and valid since 04.02.2020 to 03.02.2021 as own damage policy and from 04.02.2020 to 03.02.2023 as SCCH5 liability policy and his liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
Further submitted that, situation of the alleged accident has been twisted and petitioner was riding the motor cycle without wearing helmet and without possessing vehicle documents.
Further submitted that, petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties as the tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA 40A7095 has been involved in this accident.

Further submitted that,
driver of the offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Further he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act claim made by the petitioner is higher side, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH5 6.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1.

Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in motor vehicle accident that occurred on 01.08.2022 at about 8.45 a.m. near NH44 Road,
Hyderabad to Banga, Nandi Hobli, Chickballapura, due to rash and negligent driving of Ertiga Car bearing Reg.No.KA39DU4395 by its driver, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so how much and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. In order to prove his case, Petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 2 witnesses as PW2 and PW3 and marked 34 documents as per Ex.P.1 SCCH5 to Ex.P.34 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, R2 submitted that, he has no defence evidence.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:

sentences.text: In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chief examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of SCCH5 spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of vehicle release mahazar is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of vehicle seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.8, copy of reply notice is marked as Ex.P.9, copy of police notice are marked as Ex.P.10, copy of police intimation is marked as Ex.P.12,
copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.13, copy of PF is marked as Ex.P.14, copy of order sheet in CC No.1826/2022 is marked as Ex.P.15.
10.
In crossexamination denied that, there is no negligency of the driver of the Ertiga car.
Further denied that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the tipper lorry, further denied that, owner and insurer of the tipper lorry are necessary parties to the petition.
Further denied that, very accident is occurred SCCH5 due to his own negligency.
He admits that, car owner has paid Rs. 5,000/ for treatment.

11. Police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.15 speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver and he has admitted guilt before the Prl. Civil Judge (Jr. Dn) & JMFC Court and paid fine for the offences punishable under Sec.279 and 338 of IPC in CC No.1826/2022.

entities.text: Prl. Civil Judge (Jr. Dn) & JMFC Court
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Further it is noticed that, there is no material on record to prove the negligency of the driver of the tipper lorry.

Further it is noticed that, driver of the car had effective driving licence at the time of accident,
insurance policy was also in force.
Further it is noticed that, there is no negligency of the petitioner in causing the accident.
On the other hand, it is noticed that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.
Further there is no defence evidence either by the R1 or SCCH5 by the R2.
Further there is no dispute about accident by the driver of the car by the R1.
Looking to all these aspects this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, on the alleged place, date and time, this accident is occurred due to negligency of the car driver.
Hence I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture of the left proximal tibia fracture, for which he underwent surgery in the form of ORIF with plate and screws.

In this regard he has furnished discharge summary marked as Ex.P.16 issued by Jain Mission Hospital wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 20.08.2022 to 22.08.2022 and Xray Films are marked as Ex.P.22.
Further he has furnished estimation letter dated 16.03.2023.
SCCH5 13.
Further Dr.Nagaraj B.N., Orthopaedic Surgeon at SOADS is examined as PW2 and furnished clinical report marked as Ex.P.26 and Xray Films marked as Ex.P.27.

Further he has assessed total physical disability of the left lower limb at the rate of 40% and whole body disability at the rate of 13%.

sentences.text: In crossexamination admits that, he has not treated the petitioner, he has seen only wound certificate and discharge summary and not seen the follow up records.
Hip and ankle are normal.
He has advised for physiotherapy and removal of implants.
There is no chance of further improvement.
He has assessed only physical disability.
Further denied that, assessment made by him is premature one.
Further denied that, assessment made by him is higher side.
He admits that, he has not consulted the treated Doctor.

Further denied SCCH5 that, in order to help the petitioner, assessed the disability in higher side and created Ex.P.26 and Ex.P.27.
15.
Police papers and medical records speaks that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on left leg and he is unable to lift the weight.

Further he was inpatient in Jain Mission Hospital for 2 days,
surgery is conducted.
As per say of the Doctor, disability to the particular left lower limb is 40% and whole body disability is 13%.
it is noticed that, petitioner is aged about 26 years and factory worker.

but he has not examined the treated Doctor not produced disability certificate. Considering all these aspects functional disability to the whole body is considered at the rate of 10% which will be taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.
SCCH5 16.

Further Medical Record Technician at Jain Mission Hospital is examined as PW3 and furnished authorization letter marked as Ex.P.28, copy of MLC marked as Ex.P.29, copy of police intimation is marked as Ex.P.30, discharge summary is marked as Ex.P.31, case sheet is marked as Ex.P.32, OPD Record is marked as Ex.P.33, Xray Films is marked as Ex.P.34.

17. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 26 years, for proof of his age, he has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.17, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 25.07.1995 and the alleged accident is occurred on 01.08.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.17 his age is considered about 27 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 17 is applicable as per decision reported SCCH5 in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 18. As per his case, he was working as factory worker, thereby earning Rs.30,000/ p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.
Hence considering the same, this court relied upon the Karnataka Minimum Wages for the year 202223.

In the case on hand, petitioner is coolie,
nature of work is not mentioned in the petition, so that, he comes under the category of formerly groupIII - now semi skilled worker category.

Very accident is occurred on 01.08.2022, accordingly as on the date of accident including dearness allowances for semi skilled workers minimum wages for a month will come to Rs.14,980/, so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of SCCH5 loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under;
14,980/x12x17x10% = Rs.3,05,592/.

sentences.text:
Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/ is awarded, for loss of amenities of life Rs.15,000/ is awarded, further he is entitled for Rs.14,980/ towards loss of income during laid up period.
Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation for medical expenses SCCH5 incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.19 for an amount of Rs.56,334/.
Further petitioner is also entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards future medical expenses.

20. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1.
Loss of future income 3,05,59200 2. Pain and sufferings 15,00000 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,00000 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 56,33400 5.
Loss of amenities in life 15,00000 6.
Loss of income during laid up 14,98000 period 7.
Future medical expenses 15,00000

. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.4,36,906/ with SCCH5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.15,000/) from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

22. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.2311203277604300000 which is valid for the period from 04.02.2020 to 03.02.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 01.08.2022, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

Further driver of the car by name Shashavali had driving licence at the time of the accident, so that R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.

SCCH5 23. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,36,906/ (Rupees Four Lakhs Thirty Six Thousand Nine Hundred Six Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
(excluding future medical expenses of Rs.15,000/) from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept SCCH5 in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
